vinishkramanto, viryavanto (part. nom, sing.), for kampayan, etc.,
which coincides with the Pali and Prakrit. The same may
be said of pekshasi for prekshase + tdéva for tévat; smardhi, kur-
vahi, bhanéhi, vasdhi, for smara, kuru, bhana and vasa respectively ;
deviye and deviye for devydh ; tapasmi for tapast ; talasmin for tale ;
arhantebhih for arhadbhih + prabhaya for prabhiyd, vadchéyd for vdchd.
For tyaktvé I find the word chhorayitod, which does not seem to be
much used in Sansh rit, though Wilson, in his Dictionary, gives chhorae
na in the sense of “leaving.” I quote the following additional
anomalous forms, viz., pithitéd for pishtd, pithitant for prathitdnt,
